_note: Atrocities of war (systems/atrocities.js): salting a conquered town's fields, hostages taken before the walls and hanged when the ultimatum runs out, plague dead flung over the walls, a surrendered town put to the sword. Every act brands the player: butcher (dread, decays perDay a day) and perfidy (a broken surrender: towns refuse terms while it is at refuseAt or more). Days are game days (120 to a year).

infamy._doc: butcher: the name for cruelty; perfidy: the name for breaking a surrender. Both fall by their decay each day. refuseAt: perfidy at which towns facing you refuse to surrender and fight to the last (Sieges.termsChance and the siege's daily tick read it). lastStand: the storm defence of a town that fights to the last (x 1 + lastStand). fearPerPoint: butcher points add this to the chance of ransom and tribute (up to fearMax): a dreaded name opens purses.

labels.label: a name mothers frighten children with
no worse than any lord at war

salt._doc: Salt sown in the fields of a town you besiege or took in the last windowDays: its crops fail (world/harvests.js saltFields: yield 0, the harvest in force too) for years, the soil spent when the salt lifts. Needs salt by the town's size: out of your packs first, then the town's own market (once it is yours to take from).

hostages._doc: Townsfolk caught outside the walls (share of the people, min..max) held in your camp under an ultimatum: open the gates by the deadline or they hang. Held, every term is likelier (termsBonus) and the defenders lose moraleDaily a day; past the deadline + graceDays without a hanging the threat rings hollow (their morale +hollowMorale, your camp -hollowCamp, the bonus gone). Hanged: the defenders' morale -executeMorale, executeFlee of the garrison slips away. Released or the siege ended: they go home.

plague._doc: Corpses flung over the walls by engine: plague dead when a great plague runs within rangeHexes (the town is struck by it: systems/crises.js), else your own camp's fever dead (the flux, while the camp is sick). The town sickens (the siege's townSick: morale, garrison and people waste), its townsfolk are seeded with the illness (systems/illness.js). With the plague your own camp may catch it back (campRisk).

massacre._doc: A town that surrendered to you in the last windowDays put to the sword: popKeep of its people left, its purse (plunder x people, no more than it holds) and the market's stores (lootShare) carried off, ruins (a sack mark) and a massacre mark. The news goes to every realm: reputation everywhere, every crown's lord remembers it (data/lordMemory.json: massacre for its owner, massacre_heard for the rest), the heralds cry it. Perfidy: from now on towns refuse to surrender to you.

marks.salt: The fields of {town} were sown with salt {when} by {by}.
marks.hostages: {n} hostages of {town} were hanged before its walls {when} by {by}.
marks.plague: The dead of the {illness} were flung over the walls of {town} {when} by {by}'s engines.
marks.massacre: {town} opened its gates to {by} {when} and was put to the sword; {n} were killed.

chronicle.hostages: Hanged {n} hostages before the walls of {town}.
chronicle.plague: Flung the {illness} dead over the walls of {town}.

events.salt: 🧂 {by} sows the fields of {town} with salt.
events.hostages: 💀 {by} hangs {n} hostages before the walls of {town}.
events.plague: ☠️ {by} flings the {illness} dead over the walls of {town}.

lines.salt: Your men drag the salt across the furrows of {town}. Nothing will grow there for years.
lines.saltSiege: Within sight of the walls, your men sow the town's fields with salt. The defenders watch their future die.
lines.hostagesTaken: Your riders bring in {n} folk caught outside the walls of {town}. A herald cries the ultimatum: open the gates within {days} days, or they hang.
lines.hostagesHanged: The gallows creak before {town}. {n} hostages hang where the walls can see them.
lines.hostagesReleased: You let the {n} hostages go. They stumble back toward {town}.
lines.hostagesHome: The siege of {town} is over; the {n} hostages in your camp are sent home.
lines.hollow: The deadline has passed and no one has hanged. {town} takes heart: your threat was hollow.
lines.deadline: The ultimatum to {town} runs out today. The hostages wait on your word.
lines.plague: Your engines hurl the bloated dead of the {illness} over the walls of {town}.
lines.plagueBack: The sickness you sent into {town} finds its way back into your own camp.
lines.massacre: The gates you were opened in good faith become a slaughter pen. {n} of {town}'s people die; {plunder} gold is carried off.
